svg.title: How workloads share the machine: contention, coordination, cancellation and crash recovery
svg.desc: Independent agent workloads compete for CPU, memory, disk and GPU resources, causing slower runs, memory pressure and timeouts. A shared slot lets verification take turns while planning and editing continue. Normal execution waits, checks previous ownership, runs and retains the slot through foreground children. Cancellation releases only after proved cleanup. After a supervisor crash, a free OS lock alone is insufficient: recorded survivors or uncertain state block new work. Nested commands share the reservation; a frontend crash leaves supervised work running.

g.text: Independent agents can start resource-intensive work together
Shared slot: verification takes turns; planning and editing continue.
pnpm workload run --label verification -- pnpm check:push
03 Supervisor crash: the next caller checks survivors
OS lock released ≠ previous work finished
Invalid or uncertain state also blocks.
Never delete the permanent lock file
or signal processes from stale records.
Cooperative coordination for supported foreground groups.
Detached daemons and nonparticipating work remain outside this boundary.
